```{r}
#| label: stats
s <- jsonlite::read_json("data/site_stats.json")
# 6214 -> 6.2K, 205421 -> 205K, 173512308 -> 174M
km <- function(x) {
  if (x < 1e3) return(format(x))
  u <- if (x >= 1e6) c(1e6, "M") else c(1e3, "K")
  v <- x / as.numeric(u[1])
  paste0(if (v < 10) format(round(v, 1), nsmall = 1) else format(round(v)), u[2])
}
```

<span class="eco-status">Exploratory draft</span>

# Ecological detection data, in one format

<p class="lead">
Occupancy surveys, repeated counts, capture histories and community
detection matrices share a structure: a site or an animal carries a latent
state that is observed imperfectly across repeated surveys. **eco** puts
public deposits of all of these into one long table format, checks each
against a written standard, and versions the result so an analysis can be
rerun on exactly the data it used.
</p>
:::

::: {.eco-stats}
<div class="stat"><div class="n">`r s$n_tables`</div><div class="l">tables</div></div>
<div class="stat"><div class="n">`r s$n_deposits`</div><div class="l">source deposits</div></div>
<div class="stat"><div class="n">`r km(s$n_species)`</div><div class="l">species</div></div>
<div class="stat"><div class="n">`r km(s$n_units)`</div><div class="l">sites and individual animals</div></div>
<div class="stat"><div class="n">`r km(s$n_rows)`</div><div class="l">survey observations</div></div>
:::

<p class="eco-release">Current release: <strong>eco v`r s$eco_version`</strong> (Redivis `r s$release_redivis`, `r s$release_date`). Tables built since then are in the repository and the Redivis draft until the next release. <a href="corrections.html">Releases and corrections</a>.</p>

## Where the tables come from

```{r}
#| label: map
#| output: asis
mj <- jsonlite::read_json("data/map.json")
n_pts <- length(mj$points); n_un <- length(mj$unplaced)
cat('<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/leaflet/1.9.4/leaflet.min.css">\n')
cat('<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/leaflet/1.9.4/leaflet.min.js"></script>\n')
cat('<p id="eco-map-legend" class="eco-map-legend"></p>\n<div id="eco-map" class="eco-map" role="region" aria-label="Map with one point per table"></div>\n')
cat('<script>const MAP_DATA = ', paste(readLines("data/map.json", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), ';</script>\n')
cat('<script src="map.js"></script>\n')
```

One point per table, not per site: the mean of its site coordinates where the
table has them, otherwise the centre of the study area its description names.
Most points are therefore approximate, to the level the hover card states
(site, locality, region, state, country), and none is finer than 0.1 degree.
A ring marks a study area more than 1,000 km across, where a single point
says little. Hover over a point for the table; click it for the table's entry.

**Some locations are best guesses.** About two thirds of the tables deposit no
coordinates, and for those the point was placed by an AI assistant from the
place names in the deposit's description, then spot-checked, not verified
one by one. A point labelled region, state or country may be tens to hundreds
of kilometres from where the surveys were done. If a point is wrong, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/issues).

```{r}
#| label: unplaced
#| output: asis
if (n_un > 0) {
  cat(sprintf('<details class="eco-map-unplaced"><summary>%d of the %d tables could not be placed</summary>\n<p>Their deposits name no study area that can be located.</p><ul>\n', n_un, n_pts + n_un))
  for (u in mj$unplaced) cat(sprintf('<li><a href="data.html#%s"><code>%s</code></a>: %s (%s)</li>\n', u$table, u$table, u$title, u$basis))
  cat('</ul></details>\n')
}
```

## What a table looks like

Each row is one survey of one `unit` (a site, a camera, a sample, an
individual animal) for one `taxon`, with the observation in `y`: a 0/1
detection, a count, or a coded state. `period` and `occasion` are the two
time indices of a robust design, and covariates are prefixed by the level at
which they are constant (`unit_`, `obs_`, `period_`, `taxon_`). A row exists
only where a survey happened, so a 0 is a survey that found nothing and a
missing row is never a zero. These rows are real:

::: {#eco-specimen .eco-specimen}
:::

```{r}
#| label: specimens
#| output: asis
cat('<script>const SPECIMENS = ', paste(readLines("data/specimens.json", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), ';</script>\n')
cat('<script src="specimen.js"></script>\n')
```

## Where things stand

The [standard](standard.html) is at v1.1-draft, written against the data
structures of `unmarked`, `marked`, `spOccupancy` and the AHM code. Six
datasets bundled with R packages convert to it and back with identical arrays
and identical model estimates. The corpus is now `r s$n_tables` tables from `r s$n_deposits` deposits, covering
single- and multi-season occupancy, N-mixture and other repeated counts,
community surveys, capture-recapture (including spatial), removal and
double-observer counts, distance sampling and multi-scale eDNA; each stretch of the format is declared in the table's metadata rather
than implied by its columns. A validator that cites the standard's clauses
gates every table, CI runs it on every change, and each release is recorded
on [Releases and corrections](corrections.html).

`r s$n_below_floor` of the `r s$n_tables` tables are below the sample floor
and say so; `r s$n_experimental` are tagged experimental and may be
restructured between versions. The queue of inspected candidates is longer
than the corpus, and per-table landing pages are planned but not built.

*Tables last built `r s$built`.*
